problems.prompt: Why does corona discharge stay localized to the sharp point instead of filling the whole gap like a spark?
choices: Field lines crowd near a small-radius conductor, so only there does the local field exceed the ionization threshold while the average gap field stays low
The gas only ionizes near the cathode regardless of geometry
Corona always fills the entire gap just like an arc
The plane electrode absorbs all the field before it can spread
problems.explain: Curvature concentrates the field near the sharp tip (Peek's law sets the local onset threshold), so ionization ignites only in a small volume around the point even though the average field across the full gap is far below spark breakdown.

problems.prompt: If you shrink the electrode radius r while keeping voltage V and gap d fixed, what happens to the onset voltage needed for corona?
choices: It decreases — a sharper point reaches the local onset field at a lower applied voltage
It increases — a sharper point needs more voltage
Corona becomes impossible for any r
problems.explain: E_tip ≈ V/[r·ln(2d/r)] grows rapidly as r shrinks, so a smaller radius reaches the Peek onset field E_onset at a lower voltage — sharper points corona more easily.

problems.prompt: At higher altitude, air density factor δ drops below 1. This makes the Peek onset field E_onset ____ (increase/decrease), so corona begins at a ____ (lower/higher) voltage than at sea level.
problems.explain: E_onset = 30δ(1+0.301/√(δr)) decreases as δ falls, so thinner air at altitude ionizes more easily and corona onset voltage is lower than at standard density.

problems.prompt: A needle of radius r = 0.05 cm faces a plane at gap d = 10 cm, with air density δ = 1.0. Using E_onset = 30δ(1+0.301/√(δr)), estimate E_onset in kV/cm (to 1 decimal place).
